info.description:
Vexcel’s Application Programming Interface (API) is a set of HTTPS services that allows viewing and downloading images, elements and metadata.

These HTTPS services are defined as parameter-based REST and key/value pair protocols for requesting information. They offer responses in a wide variety of formats, including JPEG, PNG and TIFF for images and JSON/GeoJSON for metadata/elements.

Most services respond to standard HTTPS GET or POST requests, and return the information in the body of the HTTPS response. Some services require asynchronous calculations and have companion /status and /download services to retrieve the requested information.

There are several types of authentication tokens:

  • token standard auth key obtained from auth/login
  • X-API-KEY's:
    • api_key long-lived token obtained from Customer Advocacy

These tokens work with the following authentication methods:

  • Basic No authentication token - username/password
  • Bearer token
  • Cookie token or any X-API-KEY
  • Header Any X-API-KEY
  • Parameter-X-API-KEYX-API-KEY
  • Parameter-token token

To use these documents dynamically, Click the Authorize 🔓 button below and select the method you prefer.

support@vexcelgroup.com | support.vexcelgroup.com

tags.description:
Embeddings Extract

This service returns an array of embeddings in JSON format, sorted by similarity. The user can search by text, by image, or both. Alternatively they can search by location (a point).

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Retrieving semantic representations of imagery for a specific area of interest without transferring or processing raw image data
  • Enabling similarity search, classification, or clustering workflows using embedding vectors aligned to geographic locations
  • Integrating embedding data into downstream machine-learning pipelines, vector databases, or analytics systems via a single, consolidated API call

Technical Details:

This service is accessed by specifying a text string, image (as base 64 or URL) or a location. Location must be used alone - the other parameters may be combined. The response will contain an array of real-world locations (wkt polygon) sorted by each location's similarity to the input criteria. Each location represents a level 18 ortho tile from Vexcel's imagery library. The response does not include the vector IDs themselves, only the location's geometry and its similarity score. To retrieve imagery for the returned locations, use an imagery extract endpoint (e.g. ortho/extract) with the location data provided in the response.

ℹ️ Note: Search accuracy depends on how much of a collection your wkt covers.
  • Smaller areas (a small fraction of a collection) produce exact results — every candidate embedding inside the area is scored directly and always correct.
  • Larger areas (a large fraction of a collection) produce approximate results — the service ranks top candidates by similarity across the whole collection first, then filters to your wkt, so a true match may be dropped before scoring if it doesn't rank near the top collection-wide.
  • This threshold is evaluated independently per collection, so a single multi-collection request can return exact results for one collection and approximate for another. It's not fixed and may change over time, and no error or warning is returned when approximate search is used.
If completeness matters, query smaller sub-areas and combine results rather than submitting one large wkt. wkt. 		![Embedding Extract Image](https://developers.elementor.com/docs/assets/img/elementor-placeholder-image.png)

tags.description:
User Profile

This service returns a JSON file describing the content available to the account associated with the provided token or api_key. It is particularly useful for:
  • Identifying the geographic extents within which requests may be made.
  • Reviewing the virtual layers assigned to your account.
  • Determining which services are available for use.
Available Profile Information:
  • geofence – The geometry, in WKT format, defining the area within which requests may be made.
  • layers – The standard layers available for use.
  • virtual-layers – the virtual layers available for use, including settings that define each virtual layer: source layers, collect-years, max-zoom, min-zoom, and ortho-status.
  • products – The product types available for consumption for the account.
  • billing-regions – The names and geometries of worldwide billing regions.
  • service endpoints – The endpoints enabled for the account.
  • bundle settings – The restrictions defining the account’s bundle options, as specified in the customer contract.
 ![Image Profile](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/profile-query-doc.png)
tags.name: profile

tags.description:
Platform Health

This service provides a JSON file detailing the current health status of each Vexcel API service. Health checks are performed approximately every five minutes. This service is particularly useful for:
  • Monitoring the real-time health of Vexcel’s API platform.
  • Investigating potential outages or service degradations.
  • Tracking the duration of the current health state.
  • Tracking the duration of the current health state.
    • ⓘ Note: For on-demand Structure and Property endpoints (../generate, ../status and ../download) the frequency is once per day.

    Status Codes & Reasons
    • OK — The service is operating normally.
      • (no reason code)
    • DEGRADED — The service is operational but experiencing a partial issue impacting performance or functionality.
      • HIGH_LATENCY — Response times are slower than expected.
      • API_KEY_AUTH_OUTAGE — API key authentication is failing; other authentication methods are unaffected.
      • TOKEN_AUTH_OUTAGE — Token authentication is failing; other authentication methods are unaffected.
    • DOWN — The service is unavailable for all or most requests.
      • AUTH_OUTAGE — All authentication methods are failing; the service is otherwise running.
      • SERVICE_OUTAGE — The service is not running.
    • UNKNOWN — The current health status cannot be determined.
      • MONITORING_OUTAGE — The monitoring system is experiencing an issue.
    		 ![Status Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/status-query-doc.png)
tags.name: statusQuery

tags.description:
3D Tileset

This service delivers complete 3D tilesets from Vexcel’s high-resolution 3D Cities library, providing a structured collection of tiles optimized for streaming, visualization, and analysis. Unlike individual tile requests, a tileset defines the full spatial hierarchy—enabling clients to dynamically load tiles at varying levels of detail as users zoom, pan, or tilt within a 3D scene..

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Enterprise Data Integration – host or reference full 3D city datasets within internal or customer-facing applications.
  • Large-Scale Visualization – render complete city models efficiently in 3D engines such as Cesium, Unreal, or Unity.
  • Data Archiving and Sharing – provide downstream users with structured 3D datasets that include metadata, hierarchy, and spatial coverage information.
 ![3D Tileset Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/3d-tileset-doc.png)
tags.name: 3d/tileset

DTM Tile

This service will take wmts-style tile coordinates and deliver one DTM tile from Vexcel’s Digital Terrain Model.

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Modeling a Landscape
  • Mapping Hydrologic Networks (Flood/Drainage Modeling)
  • Surveying for Land-Use
  • Geomorphological Mapping

Technical Details:

This service is accessed by specifying the zoom level and tile coordinates (x,y) according to WMTS (Web Map Tile Service) specifications. The tiles returned will be WMTS-conforming, 256x256 pixels in 32-bit GeoTIFF format. Each pixel will have an elevation value in meters (over the EGM2008 geoid). 		![DTM Extract Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/dtm-tile-doc.png)
tags.name: dtm/tile

tags.description:
Embeddings Collections

This service will return coverage of collections which have been processed for vector embeddings. The response will contain the geometry of the geographic coverage for the query as well as metadata pertaining to the collection.

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Identifying the available layers for a given location
  • Identifying the available collections for a given location
  • Seeing the full extent of a collection's coverage

Technical Details:

This service operates by process of elimination to identify coverage of Vector Embedded collections; by avoiding all query parameters it's possible to receive complete coverage across the entire Vexcel Embeddings library. The layer, collection, wkt and date parameters can be used to narrow a search for specific types or locations of imagery. While this service primarily exists to provide coverage geometry, a handful of metadata attributes are also available to help identify collections. The resulting file will be in GeoJSON format.

ℹ️ Embeddings coverage may differ slightly from a collection's other product coverages (e.g. DSM or Ortho coverage).

 ![Embedding Collections Image](https://developers.elementor.com/docs/assets/img/elementor-placeholder-image.png)
tags.name: embedding/collections

tags.description:
Bundle Generate

As Bundles' single endpoint /bundle/generate service allows you to define a specific location (geofence), register it as a bundle, and receive a unique authentication token known as a geo-key. The geo-key can then be used with any Vexcel API 2.0 service for which you are licensed, providing access to data within the bundle’s predefined parameters. To authenticate other API services with a geo-key, include it in your requests using the geo-key parameter instead of token or api_key.

Put simply:
  1. Use the /bundle/generate service to create a geo-key for your desired property or location.
  2. Include that geo-key in subsequent API requests to access all content within the bundle’s geofence.
tags.name: bundle

tags.description:
Client Usage

This service returns a JSON file containing usage metrics for the specified user, group, or organization. Each unique combination of billable attributes includes the total count of usage and the corresponding unit type. This service is particularly useful for:
  • Integrating real-time platform usage data into client applications.
  • Monitoring ongoing usage to avoid unexpected billing charges.
  • Tracking usage at the user or group level.
Billable attributes:
  • {entity} – The company-name, group-name or user-name for which this metric is reported.
  • category – The type of content being counted (e.g. imagery or elements).
  • application – The specific application or service generating the usage (e.g. api, viewer or map control).
  • units – The total number of units consumed for the specified combination of attributes.
  • unit-type – The unit type used for measuring consumption (e.g. tile, element, sqkm, km).
  • region – The geographic billing region where usage occurred (e.g. united-states, eastern-europe, oceania).
  • product – The product type associated with the usage (e.g. bluesky, graysky, damage-footprints, etc.).
 ![Image Usage](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/usage-query-doc.png)

tags.description:
Embeddings Refine

Refine helps embedding/extract find more of what you want. Vote on search results ("more like this" or "less like this"), and refine turns those votes into a refinement you add to your next embedding/extract search.

Behind the scenes, the service trains on your positive and negative votes and returns the result as a search-refinement value. This service does not return search results itself; pass the search-refinement to embedding/extract to see refined results.

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Improving a text, image or location search when the first results are close but not quite right (e.g. "car" returning commercial vehicles, not passenger sedans)
  • Pushing look-alikes down the results (e.g. blue tarps showing up in a search for swimming pools)
  • Teaching the search a concept that is hard to describe in words, by voting on examples instead
  • Building human-in-the-loop review workflows, where each round of votes sharpens the next round of results

Technical Details:

Refinement is an iterative loop between embedding/extract and embedding/refine:
  1. Search: call embedding/extract with a search parameter (e.g. search-text) and include quadkey, collection and source.product-type in the include parameter. Collectively, these three fields uniquely identify each tile and are required to vote on it.
  2. Vote: call embedding/refine with the same search parameter used in step 1 (e.g. search-text) and a feedback array. Each item in the array includes the quadkey, collection and source.product-type of a returned tile and sets positive-vote to true (more like this) or false (less like this).
  3. Re-search: call embedding/extract again, passing the returned refinement in search-refinement, optionally followed by a mode (see below).
  4. Repeat: to refine further, call embedding/refine with the previous search-refinement value in the search-refinement parameter and add new votes in the feedback array. This generates a new search-refinement value, which can be passed to embedding/extract.
The refinement carries two parts, reported in the response's refinement-applied field:
  • reshape: an adjusted search vector, moved toward positively voted tiles and away from negatively voted tiles. Searching with it finds tiles the original query may not have ranked highly.
  • classifier: a model trained on the votes. It scores each matched tile and re-ranks results by that score (returned as refinement-score).
When passing the refinement to embedding/extract, append a mode to choose which part is used: {search-refinement},reshape, {search-refinement},classify or {search-refinement},all (default).
  • reshape: searches with the adjusted vector. Do not combine with other search parameters.
  • classify: keeps the other search parameters (e.g. search-text) and re-orders their matches by refinement-score. No results are removed.
  • all: searches with the adjusted vector and re-orders the matches by refinement-score.

ℹ️ Notes:
  • Use POST for embedding/extract requests that include search-refinement. The refinement is typically tens of kilobytes and grows with the number of votes, which can exceed URL length limits on GET requests.
  • Treat the refinement as a single value: pass it back exactly as received, without modifying it.
  • For best results, include at least one positive and one negative vote.
  • The classify mode re-orders only the tiles the search retrieves. On large search areas, where embedding/extract may use approximate search, use reshape or all to surface tiles the original query missed.
 ![Embedding Refine Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/embedding-refine-doc.png)
tags.name: embedding/refine

tags.description:
DTM Extract

This service returns a piece of DTM, cut from Vexcel’s high-resolution continuous orthorectified Digital Terrain Model (DTM). The same imagery you can access via dtm/tile is used to create the returned image. This service saves you the work of making multiple API calls to dtm/tile for individual tiles, stitching them together into a large bitmap, and cropping it to your specification. With a single API call you can get back a static map image matching your specified geometry.

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Generating elevation images for larger areas of interest
  • Creating 3D visualizations of terrain
  • Conducting terrain analysis for urban planning or environmental studies
  • Avoiding the need for multiple API calls to retrieve individual tiles

Technical Details:

This service is accessed by specifying the layer, zoom and wkt geometry for the desired location. The resulting image will be stitched together from multiple height-aligned DTM tiles. Each pixel will have an elevation value in meters (over the EGM2008 geoid). \

Image metadata is embedded in the headers of each image file as custom XMP tags. They can be accessed with ExifTool by running this command on the downloaded file: ```exiftool -xmp:all {filename.tif}.```<
ℹ️ Note: An error will be returned if your requested image exceeds any of the following limits:

  • An extracted image may not be comprised of more than 1,024 individual tiles (67,108,864 total pixels).
    • To maximize the imagery returned within one /extract call, your input geometry must precisely align with the Mercator tile grid at the zoom level from which you are requesting. If even a sliver of your input geometry intersects with a tile, that tile will be included in the 1,024 limit.
  • Any one image dimension (either width or height) cannot exceed 65,000 pixels.
  • The extracted image must be comprised of tiles 16 or greater. If the requested area is larger than what can be provided by zoom 16 tiles, an error will be returned.
 ![DTM Extract Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/dtm-extract-doc.png)
tags.name: dtm/extract

tags.description:
DSM Elevation

This service will return the DSM-derived elevation values for each coordinate pair in the provided wkt geometry. Compared to downloading and extracting elevation from DSM tiles, this service offers a quick and efficient way to obtain elevation data for specific locations.

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Obtaining elevation data for specific points
  • Converting 2D geometries to 3D geometries
  • Creating terrain profiles along a path

Technical Details:

This service converts a two-dimensional wkt geometry into a three-dimensional wkt geometry. For instance if a polygon is provided, this service will convert it from polygon() to polygonz(), appending a z value to each x/y pair. The z value will be derived from the underlying DSM and will returned in meters. 		![DSM Elevation Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/dsm-elevation-doc.png)
tags.name: dsm/elevation

tags.description:
Authentication System

The Authentication System Service identifies which authentication method a user is configured to use. There are two types of authentication, each with its own login service:

Traditional Login – /auth/login
Federated Login – /auth/federated-login

This service is useful for applications that support both authentication types. The client typically prompts the user for their username first. Based on the response from /auth-system, the client then directs the user either to enter their password or to complete the third-party federated login workflow.
tags.name: auth/auth-system

tags.description:
Elements Detect

Submit a location and a list of labels, and this service returns a JSON array of matching objects detected in Vexcel aerial imagery. Imagery is specified via the required images parameter. Each detected object includes the output fields requested in model-input.include — by default, a geographic geometry and confidence score; bounding boxes and pixel-level masks are available on request.

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Running targeted detection against a specific imagery collection or event
  • Integrating AI-driven object detection into downstream analysis pipelines
  • Validating or supplementing existing precomputed property and structure elements data
  • Exploring what's present at a location before committing to a full extraction workflow

Technical Details:

Supply a wkt point or polygon and a model-input object specifying the elements to detect. Each element is defined by a label (e.g., "swimming pool", "trampoline", "solar panel") and optional tuning parameters such as detection-threshold and mask-threshold. The default model is SAM 3, Meta's open-weight segment-anything model.

ℹ This service performs real-time inference. Response times will vary based on the number of requested elements and input geometry size.

 ![Elements Extract Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/elements-detect-doc.png)
tags.name: elements/detect

tags.description:
Federated Authentication

The Federated Login Service authenticates a user through a third-party identity provider (such as Google, Microsoft, Okta, etc.). Instead of providing a username and password directly, the user signs in using their external account credentials. The service then returns a new authorization token. This token is required for all subsequent API requests that need authentication. The token has an expiration time, after which the user must sign in again through the federated provider to obtain a new token.
tags.name: auth/federated-login

3D Tile

This service accepts X/Y WMTS-style coordinates and delivers 3D tiles from Vexcel’s high-resolution 3D Cities library. It is designed for third-party map viewer-type applications to render continuous 3D city content while efficiently loading only the tiles required for the current viewport.

This service is particularly useful for:

  • Urban Planning - use 3D digital twins to simulate building developments, assess shadow impacts, or optimize public spaces.
  • Infrastructure Management and Asset Monitoring - overlay IoT data on 3D city models to monitor infrastructure health.
  • Emergency Response and Disaster Preparedness - use 3D digital twins to simulate emergency scenarios, optimize evacuation routes, or plan disaster response.

Technical Details:

Content is packaged in the 3D Tiles OGC Community Standard created by Cesium, a flexible, open-source popular tile format that allows you to adapt, integrate, and interact with the data across almost any platform you work with. 		![3D Tile Image](https://api.vexcelgroup.com/v2/resources/img/docs/3d-tile-doc.png)

get.summary: Returns a file containing the metadata and geometry of intersecting graysky collection events.

post.description:
### Introduction This service will return a GeoJSON file containing graysky event coverage of oriented imagery from the Vexcel library. The output GeoJSON will contain the geometry of the geographic coverage for the query. This service is particularly useful to:
  • Identify the available layers available over a given location
  • Compare coverage between sensor types (layers)
  • See the full extent of a graysky event’s coverage
### Technical Details This service operates by process of elimination to identify graysky event oriented imagery coverage; by using no refining parameters it is possible to receive complete coverage across the entire Vexcel graysky library. The layer, aoi, and wkt parameters can be used to narrow a search for specific types or locations of imagery. While this service primarily exists to provide coverage geometry, a handful of metadata attributes are also available to help identify grayksy events.
post.summary: Returns a file containing the metadata and geometry of intersecting oriented graysky collection events.

get.description:
### Introduction This service will query the precomputed damage elements database and return a count of matching damaged properties. The response will not contain any elements objects. This service accepts many of the same parameters as damage/property/extract and operates in a very similar manner. This service is particularly useful to:
  • Estimate the potential cost of a comparable damage/property/extract request.
  • Perform market-level analysis of a neighborhood or city sized area.
### Technical Details There are a number of filtering parameters, these are booleans and defining them as true indicates that there must be a matching object in the returned property count. Alternitively, defining a filtering parameter as false means that there must not be any matching objects in the returned property count. For performance reasons this service is limited to querying for properties from no more than 10 collections in a single request. If more than 10 collections intersect the query, an error will be returned: {"status": 400, "message": "Collections list size is too big, use a smaller wkt or fewer collections"}. The 10-collection limit enables relatively large queries; in most cases an entire metropolitan area. ⓘ *This is a billable service for non-enterprise customers. Each request is reported as one billable transaction regardless of the resulting count.*

Introduction:

The /damage/property/extract service will take a WKT geometry and return a metadata response (JSON or xml) for structures with associated catastrophic damage attributes as well as some pre-damage attributes. get.description:
### Introduction This service will take x/y coordinates and deliver one vector tile from Vexcel’s precomputed Elements: Damage library. This service is intended for third party mapping applications to display continuous structure-damage geometries without the need to request each individual footprint. Structure geometries contained within these tiles will only contain those that are most-recently computed; structures from new collections will overwrite those from older collections. This service is particularly useful for:
  • Quickly assess individual properties after a catastrophe
  • Triage neighborhoods for those that are most affected by the catastrophy
### Technical Details The service is accessed by specifying the zoom level and tile coordinates (x,y) according to WMTS (Web Map Tile Service) specifications. The tiles returned will be WMTS-conforming, 256x256 pixel equivalent. All tiles will align perfectly with other Vexcel data (DSM/DTM tiles, Near-Infrared tiles, etc.) as well as tiled data from other 3rd party WMTS-conforming services. The tiles will be returned in Google Protocol Buffers (protobuf) format. Tiles are only available for zoom levels 1 - 16, zoom 16 tiles contain adequate detail even when overlaid on higher-zoom imagery.

parameters.description:
A refinement filter produced by embedding/refine. Format: sf_v{version}.{blob}[,{mode}], where {blob} is the opaque, base64url (no padding) encoded value returned by embedding/refine as its search-refinement field - it carries both the reshape search vector and the classifier, and is not meant to be constructed or inspected by hand.
version:
  • 1: the full trained SVM, including its kernel - required whenever the trained kernel (e.g. RBF) has no linear equivalent.
mode (optional, defaults to all):
  • reshape: use the blob's search vector as the similarity search vector (mutually exclusive with the other search parameters).
  • classify: re-rank the embeddings matched by the other search parameters using the classifier's decision score, instead of plain similarity. Nothing is filtered out - every match is still returned, just reordered.
  • all: apply both reshape and classify.

get.description:
The /ogc-api/api endpoint returns the OpenAPI definition document for this OGC API - Features service. The response describes all available endpoints, supported parameters, and response schemas in a machine-readable format.

This endpoint is used by OGC-compliant clients and tooling to introspect the service programmatically. The response format follows the OpenAPI 3.x specification.

The /ogc-api/collections endpoint returns a list of all feature collections available through this service. Each collection represents a distinct Vexcel dataset — such as properties, structures, or damage assessments — and is described by its id, title, spatial extent, temporal coverage, and supported coordinate reference systems.

Use this endpoint to discover what datasets are available before querying items. Each collection in the response includes a link to its items endpoint and its queryables, which describe the properties available for CQL2 filtering.

The /ogc-api/collections/{collectionId} endpoint returns metadata for a single feature collection. The response includes the collection's title, description, spatial extent, temporal coverage, and the list of supported coordinate reference systems.

The response also includes links to the collection's items endpoint and its queryables, which enumerate the properties available for use in CQL2 filter expressions. Use /ogc-api/collections to look up valid collectionId values.

The /ogc-api/collections/{collectionId}/items endpoint returns a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of items from the specified collection. Without filters, returns all items up to the collection's default limit. Results can be refined using any combination of the following:

  • bbox — spatial filter by bounding box, specified as minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat in WGS84. Use bbox-crs to supply coordinates in an alternate CRS.
  • datetime — temporal filter; accepts a single instant (2024-01-01T00:00:00Z) or a closed or open interval (2024-01-01T00:00:00Z/2024-06-01T00:00:00Z).
  • filter — attribute filter using a CQL2 expression (e.g. damage_type = 'roof'). Defaults to cql2-text syntax. Use /ogc-api/collections/{collectionId}/queryables to discover filterable properties.
  • crs — coordinate reference system for response geometries. Defaults to WGS84.

Use limit and offset together to page through large result sets. Default and maximum values for limit vary by collection.

Use the optional crs parameter to request the response geometry in a specific coordinate reference system. If omitted, geometries are returned in WGS84. Feature IDs can be obtained from the items endpoint (/ogc-api/collections/{collectionId}/items).

get.description:
The /ogc-api/collections/{collectionId}/queryables endpoint returns the set of feature properties that can be used in CQL2 filter expressions when querying items in the specified collection. The response is a JSON Schema document describing each queryable property by name, type, and any constraints or enumerated values.

Use this endpoint to discover what attributes are available for filtering before constructing a filter parameter on the items endpoint (/ogc-api/collections/{collectionId}/items). Not all properties on a feature are necessarily queryable; this endpoint reflects only those that are indexed for filtering.

The /ogc-api/conformance endpoint returns the list of OGC API conformance classes implemented by this service. Each conformance class is identified by a URI and corresponds to a specific set of capabilities defined in the OGC API - Features standard or its extensions.

OGC-compliant clients use the conformance declaration to determine which optional capabilities are available before making requests — for example, whether CQL2 filter expressions, CRS negotiation, or advanced pagination are supported.

### Introduction This service will return a GeoJSON file containing coverage of oriented imagery from the Vexcel library. The output GeoJSON will contain the geometry of the geographic coverage for the query. This service is particularly useful to:
  • Identify the available layers available over a given location
  • Compare coverage between sensor types (layers)
  • See the full extent of an AOI’s coverage

The layer, aoi, and wkt parameters can be used to narrow a search for specific types or locations of imagery. While this service primarily exists to provide coverage geometry, a handful of metadata attributes are also available to help identify AOIs.

get.description:
### Introduction This service will take a point or polygon and return one discrete image, depending on the parameters of the request. This service retrieves Nadir and Oblique Images from both Blue Sky and Gray Sky collections. Due to the broad collection specifications (multi-sensor, multi-library, multi-camera-orientation, etc.) this is a diverse compilation of data with an enormous list of potential uses, including:
  • Aerial Survey
  • Disaster Assessment
  • Engineering/Construction
  • Navigation/network planning
  • Landscape Change Detection
Use the oriented/query or oriented/collections services to query for image coverage. ### Technical Details This service is accessed by specifying a point or polygon (in WKT format). Depending on parameters, this service will return the whole image or a portion of the image. In addition to the standard GET request, this service offers the ability to overlay drawing elements (vector and text data) on imagery using POST calls. Image metadata is embedded in the headers of each image file as EXIF and custom XMP tags. The EXIF tags are readable by any common image library and the XMP tags can be accessed with ExifTool by running this command on the downloaded file: ```exiftool -xmp:all {filename.[jpg|png|tif]}.``` Not all PNG versions support EXIF metadata so for this format ONLY XMP metadata will appear. Notes on image size limits: (If your requested image exceeds any of these limits, an error will be returned.)
  • An extracted image may not be comprised of more than 1,024 individual tiles (67,108,864 total pixels).
    • To maximize the imagery returned within one /extract call, your input geometry must precisely align with the Mercator tile grid at the zoom level from which you are requesting. If even a sliver of your input geometry intersects with a tile, that tile will be included in the 1,024 limit.
  • Any one image dimension (either width or height) cannot exceed 65,000 pixels.

  • clip: Returns the smallest rectangular image that fully contains the input wkt geometry. Only the pixels that are both inside the wkt geometry and within the limits of the source oriented image will be returned; the rest will be black/transparent pixels.

post.description:
### Introduction This service will take a point or polygon and return one discrete image, depending on the parameters of the request. This service retrieves Nadir and Oblique Images from both Blue Sky and Gray Sky collections. Due to the broad collection specifications (multi-sensor, multi-library, multi-camera-orientation, etc.) this is a diverse compilation of data with an enormous list of potential uses, including:
  • Aerial Survey
  • Disaster Assessment
  • Engineering/Construction
  • Navigation/network planning
  • Landscape Change Detection
Use the oriented/query or oriented/collections services to query for image coverage. ### Technical Details This service is accessed by specifying a point or polygon (in WKT format). Depending on parameters, this service will return the whole image or a portion of the image. In addition to the standard GET request, this service offers the ability to overlay drawing elements (vector and text data) on imagery using POST calls. Image metadata is embedded in the headers of each image file as EXIF and custom XMP tags. The EXIF tags are readable by any common image library and the XMP tags can be accessed with ExifTool by running this command on the downloaded file: ```exiftool -xmp:all {filename.[jpg|png|tif]}.``` Not all PNG versions support EXIF metadata so for this format ONLY XMP metadata will appear. Notes on image size limits: (If your requested image exceeds any of these limits, an error will be returned.)
  • An extracted image may not be comprised of more than 1,024 individual tiles (67,108,864 total pixels).
    • To maximize the imagery returned within one /extract call, your input geometry must precisely align with the Mercator tile grid at the zoom level from which you are requesting. If even a sliver of your input geometry intersects with a tile, that tile will be included in the 1,024 limit.
  • Any one image dimension (either width or height) cannot exceed 65,000 pixels.

### Introduction This service will perform a coordinate transformation between world points (lng/lat) and pixel points within a oriented image. This transformation can occur in either direction:
  • world point to pixel point
  • pixel point to world point
This service is useful when identifying the exact location on Earth as represented in a oriented image’s pixel geometry or vice versa. ### Technical Details This service is accessed by specifying the transformation direction (operation), the oriented image (image-name), and coordinates (points). Because this service can transform points in either direction it is important to correctly pair the operation and point formats (e.g. if operation=world-2-pixel then points must be world points (lng, lat)). Pixel points are defined within an oriented image as the origin point (0,0) being the top-left corner of the image. Batch transformations can occur by providing more than one pair of points in a single service call.

get.description:
### Introduction This service returns a piece of imagery as a JPG or PNG, cut from the seamless orthomosaic. The same imagery you can access via ortho/tile is used to create the returned image. Ortho/extract saves you the work of making multiple API calls to ortho/tile for individual tiles, stitching them together into a large bitmap, and cropping it to your spec. With a single API call you can get back a static map image matching your specification. Notes on image size limits: (If your requested image exceeds any of these limits, an error will be returned.)
  • An extracted image may not be comprised of more than 1,024 individual tiles (67,108,864 total pixels).
    • To maximize the imagery returned within one /extract call, your input geometry must precisely align with the Mercator tile grid at the zoom level from which you are requesting. If even a sliver of your input geometry intersects with a tile, that tile will be included in the 1,024 limit.
  • Any one image dimension (either width or height) cannot exceed 65,000 pixels.
### Technical Details You can use the ortho/collections service to determine where ortho coverage exists. This allows you to know if a call to ortho/extract will succeed or fail based on image availability. Image metadata is embedded in the headers of each image file as custom XMP tags. They can be accessed with ExifTool by running this command on the downloaded file: ```exiftool -xmp:all {filename.[jpg|png|tif]}.``` ### Use Cases All use cases will ensure that imagery will not exceed either 67,108,864 pixels (e.g., 4096 x 16384) or 1,024 tiles.
  1. point wkt + zoom: This is the most common use of the service. Here you pass in a point WKT where the image will be centered and a standard zoom level. You also pass in the desired dimensions of the image you want returned.
  2. polygon wkt: Here you pass a polygon in the WKT parameter that you want covered by the returned image. The service will calculate the deepest zoom level that covers the polygon with less than the maximum number of tiles (1,024). The resulting bitmap will be fit to the minimum bounding rectangle (or MBR) for the polygon that was passed in the WKT parameter. Note that the Pixel dimensions of the resulting image are also determined by the service and cannot be specified.
  3. polygon wkt + zoom: This is very similar to the previous case, but instead of the system selecting the optimal Zoom level, you specify it with the Zoom parameter. This allows you to scale the image.

### Introduction This service will take x/y coordinates and deliver one Orthomosaic tile from Vexcel’s high-resolution multi-sensor orthorectified image library. This service is intended for third party mapping applications to display continuous imagery without the need to display large discrete images.
  • GIS Basemaps
  • Feature Digitization (tracing)
  • Natural Disaster Assessment
  • Accurate true distances and areas
  • Urban Change Detection
    •  ### Technical Details The service is accessed by specifying the zoom level and tile coordinates (x,y) according to WMTS (Web Map Tile Service) specifications. The tiles returned will be WMTS-conforming, 256x256 pixels at variable resolution (7.5cm - 20cm) in 24-bit JPEG or 32-bit PNG format. All tiles will align perfectly with other Vexcel data (DSM/DTM tiles, Near-Infrared tiles, etc.) as well as tiled data from other 3rd party WMTS-conforming services. ℹ️ *Each tile contains the header object cache-control: max-age, set to 21515 seconds or roughly 6 hours. max-age can be used by the end client to reduce the number of times the same tile is downloaded within a single user session.*

### Introduction This service will take x/y coordinates and deliver one Orthomosaic tile from Vexcel’s high-resolution multi-sensor orthorectified image library. This service is intended for third party mapping applications to display continuous imagery without the need to display large discrete images.
  • GIS Basemaps

  • Accurate true distances and areas
  • Urban Change Detection
    •  ### Technical Details The service is accessed by specifying the zoom level and tile coordinates (x,y) according to WMTS (Web Map Tile Service) specifications. The tiles returned will be WMTS-conforming, 256x256 pixels at variable resolution (7.5cm - 20cm) in 24-bit JPEG or 32-bit PNG format. All tiles will align perfectly with other Vexcel data (DSM/DTM tiles, Near-Infrared tiles, etc.) as well as tiled data from other 3rd party WMTS-conforming services. ℹ️ *Each tile contains the header object cache-control: max-age, set to 21515 seconds or roughly 6 hours. max-age can be used by the end client to reduce the number of times the same tile is downloaded within a single user session.*

### Introduction The WebMapTileService (WMTS) allows users to display Vexcel’s Ortho imagery from multiple layers in third party applications such as ArcGIS, QGIS, Global Mapper, etc. This service is based on the WMTS protocol as developed and documented by the Open Geospatial Consortium ℹ️ *This service is similar to the ortho/tile service. While both return tiled imagery, WebMapTileService uses the standardized parameters (defined by the Open Geospatial Consortium) while GetOrthoImageTile uses custom parameters specific to Vexcel’s imagery.* ### Technical Details The WebMapTileService is comprised of two operations, defined by the *request* parameter:
  • GetCapabilities - Returns an XML document that outlines the available resources and requirements of the WMTS service. Contains:
    • xml file
    • service description
    • available layers
    • image/metadata formats
    • matrix sets (EPSG codes)
    • etc
  • GetTile - Returns individual imagery tiles that conform to the WMTS specifications.
    • 256x256 pixel tiles
    • 24-bit depth
    • Variable resolution (layer dependent)
    • Image format: JPEG or PNG
    • Output format: Single image file

### Introduction This service will query the precomputed property elements database and return a count of matching properties. The response will not contain any elements objects. This service accepts many of the same parameters as property/extract and operates in a very similar manner. This service is particularly useful to:
  • Estimate the potential cost of a comparable property/extract request.
  • Perform market-level analysis of a neighborhood or city sized area.
### Technical Details There are a number of filtering parameters, these are booleans and defining them as true indicates that there must be a matching object in the returned property count. Alternitively, defining a filtering parameter as false means that there must not be any matching objects in the returned property count. For performance reasons this service is limited to querying for properties from no more than 10 collections in a single request. If more than 10 collections intersect the query, an error will be returned: {"status": 400, "message": "Collections list size is too big, use a smaller wkt or fewer collections"}. The 10-collection limit enables relatively large queries; in most cases an entire metropolitan area. ⓘ *This is a billable service for non-enterprise customers. Each request is reported as one billable transaction regardless of the resulting count.*

### Introduction This service will return a GeoJSON file containing precomputed property elements data from the Vexcel library. The output GeoJSON will contain the geometry of the parcel the parcel-based elements, and each of the parcel's structures along with their corresponding element objects. This service is particularly useful to:
  • Retrieve information about a specific property.
  • Compare information for the same property over though time.
  • Identify properties with matching attributes.
### Technical Details More than one property may be returned by this service; use the max-records parameter to prevent unexpectedly large responses. If more records are available than max-records, the order-by parameter determines which are returned and which are omitted. This is particularly important if max-records is set to 1. There are a number of filtering parameters, these are booleans and defining them as true indicates that there must be a matching object in the returned property(s). Alternitively, defining a filtering parameter as false means that there must not be a matching object in the returned property(s). The use of several filtering parameters together may cause this service to exceed the 60 second time-out; it is recommended to only use 1 or 2 filtering parameters or to reduce the size of the geospatial query. For performance reasons this service is limited to querying for properties from no more than 10 collections in a single request. If more than 10 collections intersect the query, an error will be returned: {"status": 400, "message": "Collections list size is too big, use a smaller wkt or fewer collections"}. The 10-collection limit enables relatively large queries; in most cases an entire metropolitan area. ⓘ *While the response is a GeoJSON, the structure objects are presented in a nested array one level deep. This may require additional parsing with certain JSON readers.*

### Introduction This service will return a GeoJSON file containing precomputed property elements data from the Vexcel library. The output GeoJSON will contain the geometry of the parcel the parcel-based elements, and each of the parcel's structures along with their corresponding element objects. This service is particularly useful to:
  • Retrieve information about a specific property.
  • Compare information for the same property over though time.
  • Identify properties with matching attributes.
### Technical Details More than one property may be returned by this service; use the max-records parameter to prevent unexpectedly large responses. If more records are available than max-records, the order-by parameter determines which are returned and which are omitted. This is particularly important if max-records is set to 1. There are a number of filtering parameters, these are booleans and defining them as true indicates that there must be a matching object in the returned property(s). Alternitively, defining a filtering parameter as false means that there must not be a matching object in the returned property(s). The use of several filtering parameters together may cause this service to exceed the 60 second time-out; it is recommended to only use 1 or 2 filtering parameters or to reduce the size of the geospatial query. For performance reasons this service is limited to querying for properties from no more than 10 collections in a single request. If more than 10 collections intersect the query, an error will be returned: {"status": 400, "message": "Collections list size is too big, use a smaller wkt or fewer collections"}. The 10-collection limit enables relatively large queries; in most cases an entire metropolitan area. ⓘ *While the response is a GeoJSON, the structure objects are presented in a nested array one level deep. This may require additional parsing with certain JSON readers.*

post.description:
### Introduction This service will return a GeoJSON file containing precomputed structure elements data from the Vexcel library. The output GeoJSON will contain the geometry of the structure the structure-based elements. This service is particularly useful to:
  • Retrieve information about a specific structure.
  • Compare information for the same structure over though time.
  • Identify structures with matching attributes.
### Technical Details More than one structure may be returned by this service; use the max-records parameter to prevent unexpectedly large responses. If more records are available than max-records, the order-by parameter determines which are returned and which are omitted. This is particularly important if max-records is set to 1. For performance reasons this service is limited to querying for properties from no more than 10 collections in a single request. If more than 10 collections intersect the query, an error will be returned: {"status": 400, "message": "Collections list size is too big, use a smaller wkt or fewer collections"}. The 10-collection limit enables relatively large queries; in most cases an entire metropolitan area. There are a number of filtering parameters, these are booleans and defining them as true indicates that there must be a matching object in the returned property(s). Alternitively, defining a filtering parameter as false means that there must not be a matching object in the returned property(s). The use of several filtering parameters together may cause this service to exceed the 60 second time-out; it is recommended to only use 1 or 2 filtering parameters or to reduce the size of the geospatial query.

parameters.description:
Requested Style

### Technical Details

The service is accessed by specifying the zoom level and tile coordinates (x,y) according to WMTS (Web Map Tile Service) specifications. The tiles returned will be WMTS-conforming, 256x256 pixel equivalent. All tiles will align perfectly with other Vexcel data (DSM/DTM tiles, Near-Infrared tiles, etc.) as well as tiled data from other 3rd party WMTS-conforming services. The tiles will be returned in Google Protocol Buffers (protobuf) format.Tiles are only available for zoom levels 1 - 16, zoom 16 tiles contain adequate detail even when overlaid on higher-zoom imagery.
parameters.name: style

get.description:
### Introduction This service will take x/y coordinates and deliver one vector tile from Vexcel’s precomputed Elements: Structures library. This service is intended for third party mapping applications to display continuous structure geometries without the need to request each individual footprint. Structure geometries contained within these tiles will only contain those that are most-recently computed; structures from new collections will overwrite those from older collections. This service is particularly useful for:
  • GIS basemaps
  • Neighborhood visualization

The tiles will be returned in Google Protocol Buffers (protobuf) format.

  • bbox (default for wkt): Returns the smallest rectangular image that fully contains the input wkt geometry. All pixels within the image contain data, the only black/transparent pixels are those beyond the limit of the source oriented image.
  • bbox-trimmed: Equivalent to bbox but the resulting image is trimmed down to the boundaries of the source oriented image.
  • clip: Returns the smallest rectangular image that fully contains the input wkt geometry. Only the pixels that are both inside the wkt geometry and within the limits of the source oriented image will be returned; the rest will be black/transparent pixels.
  • clip-trimmed: Equivalent to clip but the resulting image is trimmed down to the boundaries of the source oriented image.
  • full (default for image-name): Returns the full unmodified source oriented image.
  • full-bbox: Returns an image matching the dimensions of the source oriented image but only the bounding-box of the wkt selection will contain imagery, the rest will be black/transparent pixels.
  • full-clip: Returns an image matching the dimensions of the source oriented image but only the actual wkt selection will contain imagery, the rest will be black/transparent pixels.

destination-dimensions.description: Defines the dimensions (in pixels) of the output image frame. The requested region (as defined by wkt) will be centered within the image frame with two options fit or fill. Defined as destination-dimensions=width,height,fit|fill. See GET parameters for more details.

drawing.description: list of geometries in {} brackets, separated by comma. With rendering attributes for each wkt.

graysky-event.description: The event name of the Graysky collection event

image-format.description:
The file format of the image. All formats have been compressed with jpeg compression of .95.

Available values:
  • jpeg: Most performant, no georeferencing or transparency.
  • png: No georefrencing, supports transparency.
  • tiff: Least performant, supports georeferencing and transparency.
  • jpeg/png (default): Either jpeg or png may be returned. Selected automatically based on the presense of transparent pixels in the source image.
Note: rotation is applied differently based on ```image-format```:
  • ```jpeg```: Rotation is stored in the EXIF Orientation tag and must be applied by the client.
  • ```png```: Rotation is pre-applied to the image pixels; no additional interpretation needed.
  • ```tiff```: Rotation is encoded in the affine transformation matrix and interpreted by geospatial software/libraries.

interpolation.description:
Controls whether requests above the collection’s maximum zoom level may return subdivided tiles.

If true, tiles at the maximum zoom level (e.g., max-zoom=21) can be split and served as higher zoom levels (e.g., 22+). Each interpolated tile contains 256 × 256 pixels, but only the portion derived from the original data (e.g., ¼ of the tile) is counted toward billing and reporting.

If false, requests above the maximum zoom level will not return tiles.

Fields to be included in the GeoJSON result, multiple values are to be separated by commas. All nested values are returned when requesting a higher-level value. For an efficient payload it is possible to select only those objects that are important to your workflow.

  • ```precomputed```: All fields, excluding the calculated fields.

      • ```parcel-tree-cover```, ```pool```, ```enclosure```, ```sport-court```, ```hardscapes```, ```vehicles```, ```playground```, ```deck```, ```trampoline```

    • ```metadata```: Metadata about the source image
      • ```camera-technology```, ```gsd```, ```image-id```, ```capture-date```, ```metadata-version```, ```layer-name```, ```collection```, ```is-ortho-image```
  • ```calculated```: Values that are calculated at run-time. For platform performance and scalability, please request these values only if they are expressly needed.
    • ```roof-elevation```, ```roof-height```

order-by.description: The method by which to order the coverages. ```layer``` value will order the results by the order provided in the layer parameter

page.description:
Requests that would return more records than allowed by the page-size parameter are paginated. total-records and total-pages are included in the response header for page 1 only; they are not included in subsequent pages. current-page is included on all page headers. The initial request returns page 1 by default; to request page 2, append page=2 to the original request (URL or POST body) and resend.


Note: Only records in the requested pages are reported for billing. For example, if a query contains 2 pages but page=2 is never requested, only the records received in page 1 are reported for billing.

page-size.description:
Specifies the maximum number of records to return on each page of the response, up to a limit of 500. If page-size is omitted or exceeds 500, it defaults to 500. This parameter does not reduce the total number of records matching the query; it only controls how many records are returned per page. Smaller page-size values will result in more pages.


Note: This parameter is useful to prevent unexpectedly large billable requests or to improve response times.

spatial-operation.description:
The spatial-query specifies the coverage requirement over the input wkt polygon in order to return data. WKT points and lines will always use intersect and image-name in case is accepted by the service will ignore this parameter

Available values:
  • intersect: Data intersecting the input wkt will be considered
  • covers-wkt: only for data completely contained within the input wkt will be considered
  • within-wkt (default): only for data completely containing the input wkt

srid.description: The SRID code for the projection reference representing the coordinates of the given coordinates or WKT

total-records.description:
Specifies the maximum number of records to return. This parameter reduce the total number of records matching the query.


Note: This parameter is useful to prevent unexpectedly large billable requests or to improve response times.
